title: A Bowl of New England Chowder
description: Explore a familiar creamy chowder through its ingredients, serving pieces, and regional associations.
cardDescription: Explore a familiar creamy chowder through its ingredients, serving pieces, and regional associations.
subtheme: A Bowl of New England Chowder
focus: New England clam chowder commonly combines clams with a creamy base and potatoes. The clues concern that familiar style while recognizing that chowder recipes and regional versions differ.
solvingTip: Use a named ingredient before a general cooking or serving word.

Chunky soup style associated with clams and other hearty ingredients

answerNotes.CHOWDER: Chowder names a soup family; the creamy New England style is one recognizable version.
answerNotes.CLAM: Clams are bivalve mollusks, distinct from crustaceans such as crabs.
answerNotes.POTATO: The potato is a stem tuber; its familiar kitchen use differs from the shellfish ingredient.
answerNotes.CREAM: A creamy base distinguishes a familiar New England version from tomato-based Manhattan clam chowder.
answerNotes.LADLE: A ladle transfers the soup, while a smaller spoon is used for eating it.

title: Gumbo at a Louisiana Table
description: Identify familiar gumbo vocabulary through its thickening ingredients, cooking base, and rice accompaniment.
cardDescription: Identify familiar gumbo vocabulary through its thickening ingredients, cooking base, and rice accompaniment.
focus: Gumbo has varied Louisiana traditions and recipes. The clues distinguish okra, a cooked flour-and-fat base, and powdered sassafras leaves rather than treating them as the same ingredient.
solvingTip: Use the ingredient’s source or preparation to choose its name.
words: GUMBO
Louisiana stew often served with rice
ROUX
Cooked flour-and-fat mixture used as a base in many gumbos
OKRA
Green ridged seed pod used in many gumbo recipes
FILE
Powder made from dried sassafras leaves, with accent omitted
SASSAFRAS
Tree whose dried leaves supply a traditional gumbo powder
RICE
Grain commonly served with a bowl of gumbo
SHRIMP
Small crustacean included in many seafood gumbos
CELERY
Crisp stalk vegetable in a familiar Louisiana cooking base
ONION
Layered bulb chopped into many savory Louisiana dishes
PEPPER
Bell ___, vegetable paired with onion and celery in a common base
POT
Deep vessel in which gumbo simmers
SPOON
Utensil used for eating the stew
BOWL
Individual dish holding a serving of gumbo
STOCK
Flavored cooking liquid used to build a stew's base

answerNotes.GUMBO: Gumbo varies across households and traditions; the word does not prescribe one unchanging ingredient list.
answerNotes.ROUX: A roux is cooked before liquid is incorporated; its color and flavor depend on preparation.
answerNotes.OKRA: Okra is one gumbo ingredient and thickener; it is not required in every version.
answerNotes.FILE: Filé is pronounced roughly fee-lay; the grid omits the accent mark.
answerNotes.SASSAFRAS: The leaf powder is filé; it is different from a roux made from flour and fat.

title: Salsa on a Southwestern Table
description: Explore a fresh salsa through chopped produce, herbs, citrus, and familiar serving words.
cardDescription: Explore a fresh salsa through chopped produce, herbs, citrus, and familiar serving words.
focus: Salsa is a broad category with many cooked and fresh forms. The clues focus on a recognizable fresh tomato mixture and distinguish leaves, fruits, and serving vessels.
solvingTip: Use the produce description or completed food name before a short preparation word.

Sauce category including fresh tomato-and-chile mixtures

answerNotes.SALSA: Salsa means sauce and includes many forms; a fresh tomato mixture is only one familiar version.
answerNotes.CILANTRO: In American kitchen usage, cilantro commonly names the leaves and coriander the dried seeds.
answerNotes.JALAPENO: Jalapeño can be used green or ripe; heat varies among peppers rather than following one exact level.
answerNotes.TOMATO: Tomato is botanically a fruit, even though its culinary use is often savory.
answerNotes.PICO: Pico de gallo is one fresh salsa style; the clue asks for only the opening word.

title: A Southern Grits Breakfast
description: Recognize a familiar corn-based breakfast through its grains, texture, and serving companions.
cardDescription: Recognize a familiar corn-based breakfast through its grains, texture, and serving companions.
focus: Grits are made from ground corn, while hominy describes corn treated by a particular process. The clues keep those terms distinct and use familiar breakfast objects for support.
solvingTip: Read whether the clue asks for the grain product, its texture, or something served alongside it.
words: GRITS
Coarsely ground corn cooked into a familiar Southern porridge
HOMINY
Corn treated with an alkaline process that removes its outer hull
PORRIDGE
Soft dish made by cooking a grain product in liquid
COARSE
Having relatively large particles, as some ground corn does
KERNEL
Individual grain on an ear of corn
CORN
Grain crop supplying the main ingredient in grits
BOWL
Deep dish holding a breakfast serving
SPOON
Utensil used to eat a soft cooked grain dish
BUTTER
Dairy spread commonly melted into cooked grits
CHEESE
Savory dairy addition used in some grits dishes
CREAMY
Smooth and rich in consistency, as well-cooked grits may be
EGG
Breakfast item often served alongside a grain dish
MILK
Dairy liquid used in some breakfast preparations
POT
Vessel in which the grain mixture cooks

answerNotes.GRITS: Grits can be made from different kinds of corn; not every product is made from hominy.
answerNotes.HOMINY: Hominy is processed corn, distinct from ordinary cornmeal before that treatment.
answerNotes.PORRIDGE: Porridge is a broad preparation category, including more than one grain or regional dish.
answerNotes.COARSE: Coarse describes particle size rather than a particular variety of corn.
answerNotes.KERNEL: A kernel is one grain; ground kernels form products with different textures and uses.

title: Cornbread in an Iron Skillet
description: Explore skillet cornbread through its cornmeal, leavening, pan, and browned outer edge.
cardDescription: Explore skillet cornbread through its cornmeal, leavening, pan, and browned outer edge.
focus: Cornbread recipes vary in sweetness, texture, and ingredients. The clues identify a batter and its cookware without claiming one style belongs exclusively to a single region.
solvingTip: Separate the dry ingredient, the mixed batter, and the equipment that shapes the loaf.
words: CORNBREAD

answerNotes.CORNBREAD: Cornbread has many regional and household forms; sweetness and flour content are not identical in every version.
answerNotes.CORNMEAL: Cornmeal differs in grind size and is not the same ingredient as purified cornstarch.
answerNotes.SKILLET: A skillet provides the cooking vessel; cast iron is one familiar material rather than part of the definition of every skillet.
answerNotes.BATTER: Batter is typically looser than a kneadable dough, though mixtures vary in thickness.
answerNotes.LEAVEN: Leaven is a process word; baking powder and yeast work in different ways to produce rising.
